transcript.statement: Efficiency is crucial for user satisfaction and operational success. EFF-01 ensures transactions are processed within 3 seconds, fostering responsiveness. EFF-02 guarantees a minimum throughput of 100 transactions per minute, maximizing resource utilization. EFF-03 focuses on minimizing latency for transaction history access, enhancing performance. EFF-04 aligns with SAF-01 and TRU-04 by prohibiting negative balances, ensuring efficiency in transaction processing. EFF-05 prevents user delays by automatically withdrawing funds from savings accounts. EFF-06 provides immediate feedback on withdrawals exceeding balances, crucial for user experience. EFF-07 promotes effective load balancing for transaction requests, optimizing performance.

conflicts_raised.description: Requirements SAF-01, TRU-04, and RES-03 conflict with the need for efficient transactions as they focus on prohibiting negative balances, which can introduce delays in processing withdrawals, contradicting EFF-01 and EFF-05.

transcript.statement: Sustainability is essential in developing the ATM system. GRN-01 focuses on minimizing energy consumption by optimizing transaction processing, which can enhance overall efficiency. GRN-02 provides a carbon footprint report for each transaction, promoting transparency in environmental impact. GRN-03 ensures the use of energy-efficient hardware, reducing resource usage. GRN-04 emphasizes minimizing data storage requirements, aligning with sustainable data practices. GRN-05 offers clients electronic transaction records, reducing paper waste. GRN-06 supports energy savings by shutting down during inactivity. GRN-07 promotes annual assessments of environmental impact, ensuring continuous improvement.

conflicts_raised.description: Requirements EFF-01, EFF-02, and EFF-03 may conflict with GRN-01 as prioritizing speed and throughput could lead to increased energy consumption during peak loads.

transcript.statement: Safety and reliability are paramount for the ATM system. SAF-01 prevents negative balances, ensuring user trust and financial safety. SAF-02 and SAF-03 provide mechanisms for secure financial transactions, safeguarding users from overdrafts. SAF-04 ensures transaction logging for accountability, while SAF-05 secures user access with PIN verification, enhancing overall safety. SAF-06 allows for safe degradation during maintenance, and SAF-07 ensures users are informed about their account status post-transaction, which fosters reliability and user confidence.

conflicts_raised.description: Requirements EFF-04, TRU-04, and RES-03 conflict with SAF-01, as they prohibit negative balances, potentially leading to delayed transactions, which undermines user safety by increasing the risk of user frustration.

transcript.statement: Trustworthiness is critical for the ATM system. TRU-01 ensures transaction encryption, protecting sensitive data during transmission. TRU-02 establishes secure PIN authentication, safeguarding user access. TRU-03 mandates transaction logging for auditability, enhancing accountability. TRU-04 prevents negative balances, ensuring financial integrity. TRU-05 allows users to review their transaction history securely, promoting transparency. TRU-06 notifies users of insufficient funds, preventing unauthorized transactions. TRU-07 maintains data integrity by validating all operations against business rules, essential for user trust and system reliability.

conflicts_raised.description: Requirements EFF-04, SAF-01, and RES-03 conflict with TRU-04 as they focus on prohibiting negative balances, which might introduce delays, undermining the promptness in preventing unauthorized transactions.

transcript.statement: Ethical and compliance considerations are vital for the ATM system. RES-01 ensures adherence to financial regulations, safeguarding both the bank and customers. RES-02 mandates comprehensive transaction logs for accountability and transparency. RES-03 prevents negative balances to uphold fairness in transactions, protecting users from overdrafts. RES-04 enforces secure PIN authentication, ensuring user identity and trust. RES-05 limits automatic withdrawals to instances with sufficient funds, promoting responsible banking. RES-06 provides immediate notifications on insufficient funds, maintaining transparency. RES-07 ensures user privacy by encrypting sensitive data, aligning with social responsibility. These requirements support ethical practices in the banking sector.

requirements.text: The system shall ensure all accounts do not have negative balances, allowing temporary overdraft limits with strict compliance checks and mandatory user notifications.
The system shall automatically withdraw funds from the related savings account if the checking account balance is insufficient, paired with user notifications.
The system shall inform the user and terminate the transaction if the saving account balance is insufficient for the withdrawal.
The system shall log all transactions with date, time, type, amount, and resulting balance.
The system shall implement secure PIN verification for user authentication.
The system shall provide users with a clear summary of account status after each transaction.
The ATM system shall process transactions within 3 seconds to ensure user responsiveness.
The system shall maintain a transaction throughput of at least 100 transactions per minute.
The ATM application shall optimize data retrieval to minimize latency when accessing transaction history.
The ATM system shall utilize energy-efficient hardware components to operate.
The ATM system shall provide an option for clients to receive electronic transaction records instead of paper receipts.
The ATM system shall ensure that all recorded transactions are logged in a way that minimizes data storage requirements.
The system shall ensure all transactions comply with applicable financial regulations and standards.
The system shall maintain user privacy by securely encrypting all personal and financial data.
The ATM system shall provide a carbon footprint report for each transaction executed.

conflict_resolutions.rationale: The requirement to prohibit negative balances was merged into F-01 to allow temporary overdraft limits.
The requirement for automatic withdrawals was decomposed into separate notifications and transaction handling in F-02.
Temporary overdraft limits were merged to allow for energy efficiency within controlled parameters.

dropped.reason: The requirement for safe degradation during maintenance was dropped as it did not fit the synthesized goals.
Immediate feedback on withdrawals exceeding balances was dropped as it was integrated into user notifications.
Load balancing was dropped since it was not explicitly addressed in the final requirements.
The requirement to minimize energy consumption directly was dropped as it became part of the overall efficiency strategy.
